- [USER] User inquired about notable company-wide changes made by Apple's leadership in response to the pandemic.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Apple's leadership made several notable company-wide changes in response to the pandemic, including:
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Remote work: Apple announced that its employees could work remotely when applicable, with CEO Tim Cook stating that "flexibility will be key" during these times.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Retail stores: Apple closed all of its retail stores worldwide, except for those located in Greater China, and has slowly reopened its stores with health and safety precautions in place, such as mandatory face coverings and temperature checks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Donations: Apple has donated millions of dollars to COVID-19 relief efforts, including $15 million to the global COVID-19 response and $10 million to the "One World: Together at Home" virtual benefit concert.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Product development: Apple has shifted its focus to products that are useful during the pandemic, such as expanding its health features in the Apple Watch and developing a COVID-19 screening app in partnership with the CDC.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Financial assistance: Apple has offered financial assistance to its suppliers in need and has extended payment terms for small business partners, as well as provided options for customers to defer payments on their Apple Card without accruing interest.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Apple's sales numbers rebounded, with strong demand for products like the iPhone and MacBook, leading to a revenue of $64.7 billion for the fourth quarter of 2020, which was higher than expected and an increase from the same quarter in 2019.
